NONE: B1 to express your choice or opinion, especially by officially writing a mark on a paper or by raising your hand or speaking in a meeting
投票；選舉；（對…）進行表決

C: B1 [ C ] the act of showing your choice or opinion in an election or meeting by writing an X on an official piece of paper or putting your hand up

C usually singular: B2 [ C usually singular ] a way of making a decision by asking a group of people to vote
› the total number of votes given or received in an election
C1 the fact of being officially allowed to vote

example: She was too young to vote in the election.
她的年齡太小，不能在選舉中投票。
The committee voted on the proposal, and accepted it unanimously.
委員會就這一提議進行投票表決，結果一致通過。
Did you vote for or against the motion?
對這項動議你投了贊成票還是反對票？
Over 55 percent voted Democrat.
55%的選民投了民主黨的票。
[ + to infinitive ] Employees voted to accept the offer of an eight percent pay rise.
員工表決同意接受8%的工資升幅。
[ + (that) ] I vote (that) we (= I think we should) go to the cinema first and eat afterwards.
我覺得我們應該先去看電影，然後再去吃飯。
[ + obj + noun ] The evening was voted a tremendous success (= this was most people's opinion).
大部分人認為那場晚會是非常成功的。
It was the younger members who voted Smith onto the committee.
是年紀較輕的成員將史密斯選進了委員會。
The Conservative Party was voted into/out of office (= was chosen in an election to become/stop being the government).
保守黨被選上／下了台。
The suggestion was approved, with 25 votes in favour, and seven against.
25票贊成，7票反對，這項提議獲得了通過。
She cast her vote (= voted) for the Independent candidate.
她投票支持獨立候選人。
We called a meeting in order to take/hold a vote on the issue.
我們召集了一次會議對這個問題進行表決。
The party got/took 25 percent of the vote.
該黨獲得了總票數的25%。
They are trying to capture the female vote (= to persuade women to vote for them).
他們正在試圖爭取女性選民的選票。
In some countries women still don't have the vote.
在某些國家女性仍然沒有選舉權。
The proposal was read out and then put to the vote.
這項提議被宣讀，然後提交表決。

NONE: › formal an occasion when the members of a parliament or other organization are asked to say that they support the people in authority and agree with their actions
信任投票
› a sign that you are pleased with the quality of something or what someone has done or produced
滿意；信任；贊成

example: The government held a vote of confidence and lost/won it.
政府舉行了一次信任投票，結果未獲通過／順利過關。
I think the fact that so many of you are here tonight is a vote of confidence for our local performers.
我覺得今晚你們這麼多人來到這裡是對我們地方演員的一種肯定。

NONE: › an occasion when most of the members of a parliament or other organization say that they do not support the people in authority and that they disagree with their actions
不信任投票
› an act of formally and publicly thanking a person or organization for something they have done
公開鳴謝，謝辭

example: The new Chairperson stood up and proposed (= said) a vote of thanks to the retiring Chair for all her hard work.
新任主席站起來提議向即將卸任的主席所做的辛勤工作表示感謝。

NONE: › to defeat something such as a law or plan by voting against it
投票否決
› to show that you do not like or agree with something on the internet by clicking on a symbol such as an arrow or thumb pointing down
（在互聯網上表示自己不喜歡或不贊成某事時）點擊不贊成，點「踩」，差評

example: The proposal to build a new road was voted down.
修建一條新路的提議被投票否決了。
Users tend to vote down any rude or juvenile comments.
用户们对于粗鲁或不成熟的言论倾向于点「踩」。

NONE: › to accept and make possible something such as a law or plan by voting for it
投票通過

example: The committee voted through a proposal to cut the defence budget.
該委員會投票通過了一項議案來削減國防預算。

NONE: › to show that you like or agree with something on the internet by clicking on a symbol such as an arrow or thumb pointing up
（在互聯網上表示自己喜歡或贊成某事時）點贊，好評

example: If you found this article useful, please vote it up.
如果你覺得這篇文章有用，請點贊。

NONE: › US to approve or not approve something such as a law or plan by voting for it
或贊成或反對

example: The plan cannot be amended - the state legislature must either vote it up or vote it down.
這項計畫無法修改——州立法機關必須要麼贊成要麼反對。

NONE: › to show your opinion by leaving an organization or by no longer supporting, using, or buying something
用腳投票（指退離機構、不再支持、不再使用某產品等）

example: When the price of skiing doubled, tourists voted with their feet and just stopped going.
當滑雪的價格上升一倍的時候，遊客們都不願接受，所以乾脆就不去了。

NONE: › something that will win votes because it is popular with the voters
吸引選票之物

example: Her stance on taxes could be a big vote-getter in this election.
她在稅收方面的立場可能會在這次選舉中為她贏得不少選票。

NONE: C2 a person who votes or who has a legal right to vote, especially in an election
投票人；表決者；（尤指）選民

example: Of course, tax cuts are usually popular with (the) voters.
當然，減稅通常會很受選民們歡迎。
Labour voters tend to rate the National Health Service as a top priority.
支持工党的選民通常贊成把國民保健制度列為重中之重。

NONE: › the activity of choosing someone or something in an election
選舉；投票

example: Voting went ahead despite threats from rebel groups.
儘管倒戈群體發出了威脅，投票仍然照常舉行。
Pollsters asked people their voting intentions.
民意調查人士詢問人們的投票意向。

NONE: › a machine used to automatically record and count votes in an election
選票計數器；選舉計票器
› a piece of paper on which people mark who they want to vote for in an election and then put into a box in order to vote for that person
（投票時使用的）選票
› given or done to honour and thank a god
奉獻的；（向上帝）還願的
